region.text: the Eastern Army's lands, the Tokugawa camp

ledger.note: 1600: the Tokugawa win Sekigahara and begin the shogunate. 'Eastern army victory' on 21 October 1600; the battle 'is generally considered to be the beginning point of the Tokugawa shogunate, which ruled Japan for another two and a half centuries until 1868'. The Tokugawa page infobox says 'Shogunate established: 24 March 1600' (its text gives 1603). The core is the Eastern Army's lands, Cliopatria's 1600 shape; the page names provinces only for a few daimyo.

region.text: the Western Army's half, confiscated and redistributed after Sekigahara

ledger.note: 1600: the Tokugawa take the western half. 'Tokugawa clan gains nominal control of all Japan'; 'roughly 87 daimyo had their domains confiscated and their power stripped due to their support of Mitsunari'; 'Immediately following the battle, Ieyasu redistributed domains worth 6.8 million koku'; Mōri Terumoto's fiefs cut 'from eight provinces to only two provinces in Suo and Nagato'. The Toyotomi keep Osaka Castle with Hideyori.

1603: Ieyasu becomes shogun. The page cites 'Ieyasu's appointment as shogun in 1603' (the Azuchi-Momoyama page: 'Tokugawa shogunate established: 24 March 1603'); the regime begun at Sekigahara is now the formal shogunate. Same state, same colour.

region.text: Okinawa Island and the Ryukyu Kingdom

ledger.note: 1609: Satsuma lands in Ryukyu. The fleet left on 4 March and the Satsuma forces landed at Unten on 25 April (infobox 'March-May 1609'); the page says Satsuma invaded with the permission of the newly established Tokugawa shogunate.
1609: Shuri falls. Satsuma ships entered Naha harbor on 1 May and Shuri Castle was inventoried on 5 May; Shō Nei left Unten for Satsuma on 17 May. Infobox 'Satsuma victory'.

region.text: the Ryukyu Kingdom, 'a feudal dependency of Satsuma'

ledger.note: 1609: the Ryukyu Kingdom becomes a vassal. Infobox 'Ryukyu becomes a vassal state'; the 1611 oaths at Kagoshima say 'the islands of Riu Kiu have from ancient times been a feudal dependency of Satsuma'; Shō Nei met Hidetada on 28 August 1610. The Ryukyu dossier (jk-01-b) records the vassalage to Satsuma Domain; here it is the shogunate's tint, the Satsuma Domain being an Edo han. The kingdom stays nominally independent, a tributary of China.

region.text: Amami Oshima and several northern islands

ledger.note: 1611: Satsuma takes the Amami Islands. the page says Amami Ōshima and several northern islands were annexed into Satsuma Domain, without a year (the Kagoshima oaths and terms are dated 1611). Cliopatria's shape already holds three Amami cells from 1600.

region.text: eastern and south-eastern Hokkaido (Ezo) as the shape adds it

ledger.note: 1799: the shogunate controls eastern Ezo. Page silent on 1799: the Hakodate bugyō page says 'In 1779, the Tokugawa shogunate exerted direct control over Hakodate' and 'The office was created in 1802'; Cliopatria's shape adds 129 Hokkaido cells in 1799. Ainu land, no state.

region.text: the eastern Ezo cells of the 1799-1821 shape

ledger.note: 1822: eastern Ezo leaves the shape. Page silent: no page opened dates the return to the Matsumae; Cliopatria's shape for 1799-1821 ends in 1821.

region.text: Iturup and the islands to its south (Kunashiri, Shikotan, Habomai) as the 1855 line leaves them to Japan

ledger.note: 1855: the Treaty of Shimoda gives Japan the southern Kurils. 'Henceforth the borders between Russia and Japan will pass between the islands Iturup (Etorofu) and Urup (Uruppu)'; 'The whole island of Iturup belongs to Japan'. Cliopatria's shape shows them from 1856. Counterpart nobody: the Kurils were Ainu land that Russia did not hold (Japan's position: the islands 'had never belonged to Russia').

region.text: the whole of Sakhalin, undivided under the 1855 treaty

ledger.note: 1855: Sakhalin is left undivided. The Shimoda treaty said the island 'was not to be partitioned' and it stayed a joint Russo-Japanese condominium; Cliopatria's 1865 shape hands Japan the south up to 50 N, which no page supports. The zone is drawn contested.

1856: Hokkaido joins the shape. Page silent on a year: 'Towards the end of the Edo period, the shogunate often assumed control over Ezo'; Takeuchi Yasunori is Hakodate magistrate 1854-1861 (Hakodate bugyō page). The Matsumae Domain page also says 'In 1599, submission to Tokugawa Ieyasu led to the recognition of the right to rule over Ezo' and a black seal of 1604 gave trading rights with the Ainu, a nominal claim that Cliopatria does not draw before 1856.

region.text: the western and central domains that go over to the Meiji government

ledger.note: 1868: the Restoration takes the western domains. Infobox 'Meiji Restoration: 3 January 1868'; the page says loyalist retainers kept fighting. The land is Cliopatria's Empire of Japan 1868 shape (229 western cells); the page names no domains.

1868: the shogunate's tint on the Ryukyu Kingdom ends with the shogunate. The Ryukyu dossier has the Satsuma vassalage run to October 1872, under Meiji; the page opened here does not mention Ryukyu in 1868.

region.text: Sakhalin, passed to the Empire of Japan

ledger.note: 1868: the shogunate's claim to Sakhalin passes to the Meiji state, which exchanges it for the Kurils in 1875 (Kuril Islands dispute page: Japan gives up Sakhalin in exchange for Russia giving up the Kuril Islands).

region.text: the shogunate's remaining land, passed to the Meiji state

ledger.note: 1868: the Tokugawa shogunate ends. Infobox 'Meiji Restoration: 3 January 1868'; the shogunate 'came to an official end in 1868' with Tokugawa Yoshinobu's resignation; succeeded by the Empire of Japan. The loyalist side, defeated at the Battle of Hakodate 'in June 1869', is the unresolved Boshin War remainder.

wars.name: Invasion of Ryukyu
wars.outcome: Satsuma victory: Ryukyu becomes a vassal state, pays tribute, accepts the Fifteen Injunctions; the Amami Islands are annexed into Satsuma Domain.
wars.note: The page frames the invasion as a punitive mission by Satsuma with the permission of the newly established Tokugawa shogunate; infobox March-May 1609.

wars.name: Shakushain's revolt
wars.outcome: 'In 1669, what began as a dispute over resources between rival Ainu clans escalated into a rebellion against Matsumae control. It lasted until 1672, when Shakushain's revolt was finally put down.'
wars.note: Fought by the Matsumae clan; no change in the outline.

wars.name: Menashi-Kunashir rebellion
wars.outcome: 'The last serious Ainu rebellion was the Menashi-Kunashir rebellion in 1789.'
wars.note: Eastern Ezo; the outline of the time (1609-1798) does not include it.

wars.name: Boshin War

zones.text: the loyalist-held lands of 1868, Edo and the north-east, and Hokkaido to June 1869

wars.outcome: Loyalist retainers kept fighting after the Restoration and were defeated at Toba-Fushimi (undated on the page); the Republic of Ezo was defeated at the Battle of Hakodate 'in June 1869'.
wars.note: The Boshin War page was not opened (page budget): this entry is as thin as the Tokugawa page.

certainty.note: Island Japan's frontier is the sea; the Ezo frontier with the Ainu and the Ryukyu relation are loose; the han boundaries inside are not territory. Ryukyu (from 1609) is a vassal, not a border.
Treaty of Shimoda Article 2 fixes the Russo-Japanese line between Iturup and Urup; Sakhalin stays undivided (soft) and the Hokkaido interior is not surveyed on any page.

notes:
Written by Phase B agent jk-01-c on 2026-10-18. Pages opened for this state (budget 5): Tokugawa shogunate, Invasion of Ryukyu, Matsumae Domain, Kuril Islands dispute, Hakodate bugyō; Battle of Sekigahara, Matsumae clan and Azuchi-Momoyama period were opened for warring-states-japan and are shared (one over the budget in effect). The Boshin War, Sakhalin and Ezo pages were not opened.

Cliopatria corrections: (1) the Ryukyu Islands (Okinawa, ten cells) are inside every shape from 1600 although the Ryukyu Kingdom was independent until Satsuma's 1609 invasion and stayed a separate kingdom (a vassal, tributary to China) afterwards; Cliopatria's own Ryukyu Kingdom row stops in 1520, so the shogunate row stood in for it. Every keyframe therefore subtracts Okinawa, and the vassal events carry the lighter tint; the Amami Islands (three cells) are subtracted until 1609. (2) 1600-1601: the shape is the eastern half only; the page says the Tokugawa gained 'nominal control of all Japan' on 21 October 1600, so a new keyframe tokugawa-shogunate_1601 draws the whole archipelago (the western half is the warring-states-japan 1600 shape). (3) 1865-1867: southern Sakhalin (151 cells) has no support: the 1855 treaty left Sakhalin undivided; it is a contest zone with russian-empire, not land. (4) 1868-1869: the shogunate ended on 3 January 1868; the 1868 shape is kept for 1868 as the war's front line, and the 1869 year is not the shogunate's.

Not settled for lack of pages: the 1799 and 1822 Ezo changes (the Hakodate bugyō page says 'In 1779'; no page opened has 1799 or 1821); the Hokkaido and Kuril extent of 1856 beyond the Shimoda line (Hokkaido rests on undated 'often assumed control'); the Boshin War course (Edo's surrender, the Northern Alliance, the Republic of Ezo from December 1868). The Tokugawa page infobox gives 'Shogunate established: 24 March 1600' while its text and the Azuchi-Momoyama page give 1603 for the shogunate; the dossier starts on 21 October 1600 (Sekigahara) and has the 1603 rename. No infobox area exists on the pages opened, so Cliopatria's 328,728 km2 (Japan without Hokkaido) could not be compared.

Counterparts needing dossiers or a decision: satsuma-domain (used by the Ryukyu dossier; the han are internal units here and the Ryukyu vassal events use ryukyu-kingdom as counterpart); matsumae-domain; the Ainu of Ezo, Sakhalin and the Kurils (counterpart 'nobody' here); the Boshin War loyalist side, namely the Ōuetsu Reppan Dōmei (Northern Alliance, 1868) and the Republic of Ezo (December 1868 to June 1869), rebel states against empire-of-japan; the Empire of Japan dossier should take 1869. Gazetteer: 'Amami Islands' is not a region name (a coordinate circle is used); 'Kanto' is not an entry either.
